claims.text: sap oxidizes into black resin; forms on skin, clothing, tools

claims.quote: the black lacquer that results from oxidation of the oleoresin after contact with the plant develops within hours of exposure and precedes allergic contact dermatitis, in some cases by weeks.

claims.text: cannot be washed off; falls off in 1 to 2 weeks; similar to Japanese lacquer
claims.quote: Notably, the lacquer cannot be washed off with soap and water and typically falls off in 1-2 weeks. This lacquer is similar to the lacquer created from Japanese lacquer trees

claims.text: accompanied by irritant dermatitis of varying severity

claims.text: isopropyl alcohol then copious rinsing more effective than soap
claims.quote: If available, isopropyl alcohol applied liberally followed by copious rinsing with water after contact is more effective than soap for preventing allergic contact dermatitis.

claims.text: bleach inactivates urushiol; organic solvents extract it
claims.quote: Bleach rapidly inactivates urushiol on clothing and tools, and organic solvents (alcohol, gasoline, acetone) can extract it from contaminated surfaces.

claims.text: prednisone 0.5 to 1 mg/kg daily for 5 to 7 days

claims.text: no evidence for long-acting injectable steroids

claims.quote: If allergic contact dermatitis involves an extensive area of skin (greater than 20 percent), systemic steroid therapy is often required and offers relief within 12 to 24 hours.
